from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the

signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If

properties.areaDesc: Southern Kenai Mtns
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 15 at 8:59PM AKST until November 16 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Additional snow accumulations between 1 and 4 inches.
Winds gusting as high as 20 mph.

* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Ice
accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering cold air is keeping precipitation
all snow. As such, the Advisory has been extended again.
Precipitation will very likely change over to rain overnight,
though there remains a 25 to 35 percent chance for a brief period
of freezing rain during this transition period.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

to 1 inch.

* WHERE...Anchorage / Eagle River (all elevations).

* WHEN...Until 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially

surfaces.

properties.areaDesc: East Turnagain Arm; Portage
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 15 at 8:59PM AKST until November 16 at 1:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Additional snow accumulations
up to 2 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...East Turnagain Arm, including Portage Valley and Girdwood.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Light ice accumulations may result in a few localized power
outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warm air aloft is transitioning snow to rain
showers. As surface temperatures are below freezing in many
locations, falling rain may freeze on contact and create icy
surfaces. Surface temperatures are unlikely to warm above freezing
overnight, so the Advisory has been extended to Monday afternoon,
when surface temperatures will be warm enough to end the threat of
icing from freezing rain.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 15 at 9:54PM PST until November 16 at 11:53AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Sunday the stage was 16.7 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM PST Sunday was 17.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Monday morning and remain below flood stage through the week.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 600 AM PST.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 15 at 10:48PM CST until November 17 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 8
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 15 at 8:45PM PST until November 16 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to
15 feet increasing to 15 to 18 feet with local sets to 20 feet.
Dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM to 9 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The High Surf Advisory may need to be
extended through Wednesday, and another round of larger surf is
expected Thursday into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

forecast.

cabins, oil field tanks and pumps are affected, and livestock

properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 15 at 7:43PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM EST Sunday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 1100 AM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Western Capes
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 15 at 2:19PM AKST until November 17 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions possible. Total snow accumulations of 1
- 3 inches possible. Winds could gust as high as 65 mph, reducing
visibility to one quarter mile or less.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, Nunivak Island, Good News Bay and
Platinum

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Very strong winds could
cause extensive damage to power lines. Visibilities reduced to one
quarter mile or less due to blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong Bering storm arrives at the Southwest
Coast on Tuesday, bringing a long duration of gusty southerly
winds. Temperatures are expected to warm Wednesday morning,
allowing for a transition to mixed precipitation.
properties.instruction:
A Winter Storm Watch for blizzard conditions means there is a
potential for falling and/or blowing snow with strong winds and
extremely poor visibilities. This can lead to whiteout conditions and
make travel very hazardous.

NWSheadline: WINTER STORM WATCH IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH TUESDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 15 at 2:17PM AKST until November 18 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels of 1.0 to 3.0 feet
above the highest tide line possible.

* WHERE...Kipnuk and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...3 AM to 9 AM Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration of gusty southerly winds
will move through the Kuskokwim Coast on Tuesday. Winds turn
more south to southwesterly Wednesday, increasing the potential
for elevated water levels, high surf, and coastal erosion. The
winds will coincide with the high tide on Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM LATE TUESDAY NIGHT THROUGH WEDNESDAY MORNING

25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock
people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid
ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

inches between 5,000 and 8,000 feet. Snow accumulations of 18 to 36
inches between 8,000 and 9,500 feet with locally higher totals
along the ridgeline. Winds could gust as high as 50 mph.

hazardous conditions could impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and
power lines.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...From Monday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Western Siskiyou County; South Central Siskiyou County; North Central and Southeast Siskiyou County
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 15 at 10:22AM PST until November 19 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations between 8 and
14 inches possible above 4000 ft, with 2 to 5 inches possible down
to 3500 ft.

* WHERE...Elevations above 3500 ft in Siskiyou County, including
Highway 89 at Snowman Summit and Dead Horse Summit, Highway 3 at
Scott Mountain Pass, Etna Summit on Sawyers Bar Road, Highway 97 at
Grass Lake, and the Interstate 5 corridor around Mount Shasta City
and Black Butte Summit.

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening through late Wednesday night. Heavy
snow may impact the Wednesday morning commute.

* IMPACTS...Travel could become difficult, or at times impossible
over higher passes. The hazardous conditions could impact the
Wednesday morning and evening commutes. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

worsen this afternoon with breaking waves reaching 25 to 30 ft.
Dangerous surf conditions persist into Monday morning. Waves
and surf remain hazardous Monday, but gradually diminish through
Monday evening.

* WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County
Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and
Brookings.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very
hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves
will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas.
Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be
expected.

and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties, piers, and other waterside infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream  also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
